docs.purpose: A single scrollable list of every pipeline run the system has recorded — what ran, when, whether it finished, and the per-run detail the pipeline itself wrote into its records_meta summary. Operators use it to answer 'did the nightly work actually happen, and what did it do' without opening a database client. It also covers the older sync_runs ledger, so the two histories read as one timeline.
docs.data_story: Nothing is built yet, so nothing is measured here. As specified it would read `pipeline_runs` and `sync_runs`.
docs.under_126: **NEW.** It does not exist; it is generated from descriptors from its first commit, through the LIST renderer (a collection with declared pagination, recycling and empty/offline states). It is **100% generated** — which is the point: if the descriptor set is incomplete or an archetype profile is wrong, this page is visibly empty or visibly wrong on commit 1, and cannot be faked by hand.

rls_class.why: Spec 114 §2 is definitional — everything that is not one of the 10 named Class-A tables, not profiles and not Class D is Class B by default, including tables added after that spec was written, which covers pipeline_runs and sync_runs — both named outright in Spec 114 §4's representative Class-B list. Class B is ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with zero policies, and per Spec 114 §4 Decision D1 the Next.js admin route connects as the table owner, so it is outside RLS enforcement entirely.

checks.why: records_meta is free-form JSONB written by 27 different steps; a row whose meta no longer parses must render as schema_drift rather than as an empty detail panel.
The LIST profile requires it, and an empty ledger means the chain did not run — the single most important thing this page can say.
The LIST profile requires an offline state; a desktop admin page keeps no cached projection, so this is descriptive and no threshold could bound it.
A failed fetch must not render as "no runs".
chain/status/since are parameters of a stable key array, never an object literal rebuilt each render.
Spec 126 §3.1 row A: the admin renders pipeline_runs UNMODIFIED — it may reveal more columns but may not derive a new one, so the surface whitelist must set-equal the contract projection.

Permanently non-zero: a chain whose newest row is older than its declared cadence is an expected, recurring operator signal, not a defect of this page. Retighten condition is a scheduled-cadence declaration per chain.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pipeline_runs WHERE duration_ms < 0 OR (completed_at IS NOT NULL AND completed_at < started_at)
invariants.why: A run that finished before it started is a clock or a write-order defect, and rendering it as a row would launder a broken ledger into a plausible timeline.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pipeline_runs WHERE status <> 'running' AND completed_at IS NULL
invariants.why: A terminal row with no completed_at cannot be ordered on a timeline, and the page would silently drop or mis-place it.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pipeline_runs WHERE status = 'running' AND started_at < now() - interval '6 hours'
plausibility.why: Stranded `running` rows are a measured, recurring condition in this estate and today they are only reaped as a side effect of a human loading GET /api/admin/stats — the page must show the number rather than let a page-load hide it.

limitations.what: The LIST required-field profile in Spec 126 §3.1 mandates list.item_archetype, list.pagination and list.recycling, and surface.schema.json has no property for any of them (the top level and every category are additionalProperties:false).
limitations.measured: Every allOf block in scripts/surfaces/_schema/surface.schema.json is `"then": true` — the archetype profiles are declared in prose in Spec 126 §3.1 and enforced by nothing, so these fields can neither be declared here nor caught missing.

limitations.what: The stranded-`running` count this page renders can be reaped out from under it by an unrelated page load.
limitations.measured: docs/reports/2026-09-15-spec126-admin-best-in-class.md §2.1 — reapStaleRunningRows() is called from exactly one site, GET /api/admin/stats:189, so the number moves when a human opens a different admin page rather than when a job runs.
